title: Cycle slotting atelier and shadow staffing simulator
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: We repeatedly over-allocate engineers to high-visibility launches and under-utilize cross-functional skills mid-cycle. This causes mid-cycle panic scope cuts and misuse of surge lanes. Goal: build a lightweight simulator + workshop (atelier) to evaluate slotting strategies, shadow-rosters, and cross-skill swaps so PMs and Eng leads can make defensible scope/staffing decisions. Deliverables: (1) interactive simulator (spreadsheet + simple web UI) that models FTE slotting, skill overlaps, soft freeze windows, and probability of spill; (2) an atelier facilitation guide and one-pager playbook for cycle planning meetings; (3) a short experiment run on two upcoming initiatives to validate outputs against historical burn rates.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator accepts: team roster, role tags, effort estimates, commit probability and outputs utilization, oversubscribe risk, and suggested two-level mitigations
Simulator produces a recommended ‚safe scope‘ and ‚surge buffer‘ size for a given cycle with configurable conservative/ambitious modes
Atelier guide includes a 45-minute facilitation script, decision matrix, and two example run-throughs using current initiatives
Run experiment on 2 initiatives and capture outcomes in the cycle dashboard; differences between simulator prediction and actuals within 20% for utilization estimates
PM sign-off on playbook and Eng leads adopt the shadow-roster approach for the pilot cycle

decision_log: Model choice: deterministic spreadsheet with Monte Carlo option — chosen for interpretability and easier audit during planning
Scope: keep web UI optional for pilot; primary deliverable is the spreadsheet + playbook to maximize adoption speed
Surge buffer rule: recommend min(10% of committed FTE, 1 full role) for orgs under 15 engineers; allow manual override
Cross-skill tagging: adopt three-tier tags (primary/secondary/backup) rather than a continuous skill score for clarity during atelier runs
